PRAKAS
ON
CONDITIONS FOR ASSET MANAGEMENT INSTITUTION
The Governor of the National Bank of Cambodia
- With reference to the Constitution of the Kingdom of Cambodia;
- With reference to the Royal Decree NS/RKT/0723/1675 of July 29, 2023 on the
appointment of Her Excellency Chea Serey as Governor General of the National Bank of
Cambodia, equivalent to Senior Minister;
- With reference to the Royal Kram NS/RKM/0196/27 of January 26, 1996 promulgating the
Law on Organization and Conduct of the National Bank of Cambodia;
- With reference to the Royal Kram NS/RKMl1206/036 of December 29, 2006 promulgating
the Law on the Amendment of Article 14 and 57 of the Law on Organization and Conduct
of the National Bank of Cambodia;
- With reference to the Royal Kram NS/RKM/1199/13 of November 18, 1999 promulgating
the Law on Banking and Financial Institutions;
- With reference to the Prakas N° 87-017-344 Prokor dated December 1, 2017 on Credit
Risk Grading and Impairment Provisioning;
- Pursuant to the recommendation made by the National Bank of Cambodia Management
meeting on January 20, 2026
Decides
Chapter I
General Provisions
Article 1.-Purpose
This Prakas aims to establish a regulatory framework for Asset Management Institution
through acquisition and management of Non-Performing Loans and collaterals from Banks
and Financial Institutions.
Article 2.-Scope
This Prakas is applicable to Asset Management Institution, hereinafter referred to as "AMI"
and Banks and Financial Institutions under National Bank of Cambodia (NBC)'s supervisory
authority, hereinafter referred to as "BFls".

Article 3.- Definitions
For the purpose of this Prakas, the following terms are defined as follows:
Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) refers to loans that are classified as "sub-standard",
"doubtful", or "loss", in accordance with Prakas on Credit Risk Grading and Impairment
Provisioning.
- Asset Management Institution (AMI) refers to an institution that is licensed by the
NBC to operate in accordance with the regulatory framework of this Prakas.
Non-Performing Loan Management refers to the process of resolving NPLs through
various methods, including debt recovery, debt transfer, debt to equity conversion, debt
restructuring or by other means with the approval of the NBC.
- Associated Collateral refers to assets or other rights directly attached to NPLs,
including but not limited to immovable properties, movable properties, and other
assets, whether held by the debtors or related third parties.
Board of Directors refers to the group of individuals who are comprised of directors
being responsible for overseeing the management and operation of the Institution on
behalf of the shareholders.
Senior Management refers to the executive management of the AMI responsible and
accountable to the Board for the sound and prudent day-to-day management of the
AMI, generally including, but not limited to, C-level Executives or equivalents and
heads of functions/departments or equivalents such as head of compliance and head
of internal audit.
Chapter II
Business activities
Article 4.- Permissible Activities
The licensed AMI may engage in the following business activities:
- Acquires and manages NPLs including associated collaterals from BFls
- Acquires and manages immovable properties of the BFls' debtor through auction by
court order or provisional administration or liquidation process;
Provides debt collection services to BFls;
Facilitate to sell associated collaterals with the debtor's consent;
Sell loan to BFls and other AMls; and
- Any other business activities as prescribed by the NBC.
Article 5.- Impermissible Activities
The AMI is prohibited from carrying out the following activities:
Provides loans or refinancing;
Provides loans guarantee;
- Acquires NPLs from BFls that have provided lending facilities to the AMI, directly or
indirectly; and
- Any other business activities that are prohibited by the NBC.
2

Chapter Ill
Licensing Application Procedures
Article 6.- Formation of the Institution
Any persons applying for AMI license shall register as a Public Limited Company.
Article 7.- Minimum Registered Capital
The AMI shall have a minimum registered capital of KHR 200 billion (two hundred billion riels).
Article 8.- License Application
Any persons applying for AMI license from the NBC shall submit the following documents:
1. Registered name or business name and address;
2. Evidence of fully paid registered capital and source of fund;
3. Legal form, Memorandums and Article of Associations, and other related documents;
4. Organizational management structure;
5. Description of shareholders and the size of their shareholdings and the evidence of
their capabilities, experience and fitness and propriety of business management;
6. Description of directors and senior management as well as the evidence that verifies the
person has good reputation, qualifications, and appropriate experience to handle NPLs;
7. First 3 (three) financial years business plan and strategies for sustainable business
operation;
8. NPLs acquisition, management and resolving strategies plan;
9. Description of IT system for a secure business operation;
10. Detailed policy on resolution of consumer complaints; and
11. Internal audit procedures.
The NBC may require AMI for other relevant documents as deemed necessary for assessing
the application.
Article 9.- Shareholding in AMI by BFls
Any BFls, either directly or indirectly, seeking to acquire or hold equity interest in AMI shall
obtain prior written approval from the NBC.
Chapter IV
Licensing Approval and Related Fee
Article 10.-Application Review and License Issuance
The NBC shall provide written notification of its decision to issue or not issue the license within
6 (six) months from the receipt of the license application.
The NBC shall set out conditions and timeline for the implementation of the approval in principle.
If the applicant fails to comply with those set conditions and timeline, the approval in principle
shall be waived, except when an extension has been requested and approved by the NBC.
3

The NBC shall grant a license after the applicant has fulfilled all conditions stated on the
approval in principle and other related procedures.
Article 11.-Term of License
The license is valid for 5 (five) years and can be renewed. AMI shall apply for license renewal
at least 6 (six) months prior to the expiration of the license date.
Article 12.-Other Approval Requirements
The AMI shall obtain prior approval from the NBC, in case of the followings:
Changing the name or address;
Increasing or decreasing registered capital;
Changing Memorandum and Articles of Association;
Changing the Board of Directors or Senior Management; and
Merging, transferring, or selling partially or in full of shares or any changes, and other
issues required by the NBC.
Article 13.-Annual License Fee
The AMI shall pay KHR 50 million (fifty million riels) for annual license fees before January
15th of each year. The AMI that has been granted license approval within the year shall pay
the annual license fee as below:
Semester 1: Pay in full year
Semester 2: Pay for one semester.
Article 14.-Other fees
The AMI shall pay other fees as follows:
Information Fee: KHR 500,000 (five hundred thousand riels);
Processing Fee or License renewal: KHR 2,500,000 (two million and five hundred
thousand riels);
Changing Memorandum and Articles of Association fee: KHR 1,000,000 (one million riels)
per page;
Changing license fee: KHR 2,000,000 (two million riels);
- Transferring shares or increasing registered capital fee: 0.5% (Zero-point five percent)
of value of share transferred or increased; and
Decreasing registered capital fee: 1% (one percent) of value of share decreased.
ChapterV
NPLs Transfer
Article 15.- NPLs Acquisition
The AMI shall acquire NPLs through transparent and arm's length transactions with the price
agreed between parties.
4

Article 16.- Rights and Obligations of AMI
Upon the acquisition of NPLs, the AMI shall have the following rights and obligations:
1. The right to enforce claims against any debtors and guarantors in accordance with the
applicable laws and regulations;
2. The right to receive all collaterals and security interests associated with the acquired NPLs;
3. The Obligations to credit reporting of information as stated in Prakas on Credit
Reporting; and
4. The acceptance/undertaking/assumption of all rights, title, interests, and obligations of
the creditor, fully and irrevocably, effective as of the date of acquisition.
In case the AMI intends to sell loans to BFls and other AM ls, the AMI shall obtain prior approval
from the NBC.
The NBC may determine other obligations as deemed necessary.
Article 17.- Rights and Obligations of BFls
Upon disposal of NPLs to AMI, the BFls shall obtain prior approval from the NBC by attaching
the following documents:
1. Requested letter on selling NPLs;
2. Board resolution;
3. Valuation documents on NPLs to be sold; and
4. Other documents required by the NBC as deemed necessary.
In addition, the BFls shall transfer all related original loan documents, including but not limited
to, loan agreements, collateral documents and repayment history to the AMI and officially
notify customers and credit reporting service provider regarding those NPLs transfer.
The NBC may determine other obligations as deemed necessary.
Article 18.- Debt Collections
The AMI shall establish a Code of Conduct governing all debt collections, which must adhere
to the highest standards of professionalism and integrity, that all debt collection activities must
comply with applicable laws and regulations related to consumer protection, data privacy, and
professional secrecy. The AMI shall ensure that all staff involved in debt collection shall
receive regular training on this Code of Conduct.
Article 19.- Resolution of Consumer Complaints
The AMI shall establish responsive mechanism and resolve all consumer complaints in
compliance with the Prakas on Resolution of Consumer Complaints.
Chapter VI
Prudential Requirement and Examination
Article 20.- Minimum Registered Capital
Before commencing its operation, the AMI shall pay 100% (one hundred percent) of its
registered capital into the account maintained with the NBC.
5

The AMI shall deposit 5% (five percent) of its registered capital as capital guarantee into its
account maintained with the NBC.
Article 21.- Prudential Requirements
The AMI shall implement prudential requirements, as may be prescribed in separate Prakas.
Article 22.- Reporting Requirement
The AMI shall prepare and submit the following reports:
Financial Statement prepared in accordance with Cambodian International Financial
Reporting Standard (CIFRS)
Report on NPLs Portfolio and Recovery by using the reporting templates attached in
Appendix and
Other reports required by the NBC as deemed necessary.
The AMI shall submit these reports on a quarterly basis to the NBC no later than the 15th day
offirst month of the next quarter. The AMI shall be liable for ensuring the accuracy of all reports
submitted to the NBC.
Other than the above reports, the AMI shall submit the audited financial statement to the NBC
no later than on the 30th of April of the following year.
Article 23.- Professional Secrecy
The AMI shall implement the provision of professional secrecy as follows:
- The Board of directors, Senior management, and all other staffs of the AMI shall not
disclose any confidential information or data which they might have become aware
through their functions.
- Any person who fails to observe this obligation of professional secrecy shall be liable
to the sanctions in compliance with the Law on Banking and Financial Institutions.
- The obligation of professional secrecy shall not be used as a ground for nondisclosure
vis-a-vis the supervisory authority, auditors, provisional administrators, liquidators, or
a court dealing with criminal proceedings.
Article 24.- Record Keeping
The AMI shall maintain all transaction-related documents, accounting and financial records,
and electronic system records for examination by the NBC. These documents and records
shall be maintained for a minimum of 10 (ten) years from the date of the final resolution of the
NPLs, including collaterals.
Article 25.- Examination
The AMI is under the NBC's supervisory authority. The NBC may examine the AMI at any time
with or without prior notice.
The AMI shall provide any documents and records requested by the NBC for the examination
purpose at such timeline set out by the NBC.
The NBC may require the AMI to take all necessary measures in case the AMI is violating
related regulations.
6

Chapter VII
Governance
Article 26.- Composition of Board of Directors
The AMI shall have 5 (five) board members with at least 2 (two) independent members.
Article 27.- Qualification of Board of Directors and Senior Management
Board of Directors and senior management of AMI shall have adequate qualifications of banks
and financial systems and competent knowledge of relevant laws and regulations to
understand any issues that may arise. No one shall be a member of the Board of Directors
and senior management of AM I if he has been convicted of:
- A crime;
- Thef, fraud or breach of trust;
Usury;
Money laundering and financing of terrorism; or proliferation financing of weapons of
mass destruction;
Issuing checks with insufficient funds in the account; and
Bankruptcy, receivership, or liquidation of assets.
Board members and senior management who are appointed shall seek prior approval from
the NBC.
Article 28.- Board of Directors Responsibilities
Board of Directors shall approve and periodically review strategies, policies, and procedures
related to operations and risk management. Board of Directors shall ensure that policies and
procedures are implemented effectively.
Board of Directors shall approve the business plan and establish Audit Committee, Risk
Management Committee and Committee to oversee NPLs acquisition. Board of Directors may
establish other committees as deemed necessary or as required by the NBC.
Board of Directors shall establish compliance, internal audit, and legal functions to ensure that
these functions have sufficient and qualified human resources to fulfill their duties.
Board of Directors shall conduct meetings at least 4 (four) times per year, and the AMI shall
provide the agenda of each meeting to the NBC in advance. In circumstances where deemed
necessary, the NBC may participate in the meetings as an observer.
Article 29.-Senior Management Responsibilities
Senior Management is responsible for implementing policies, procedures, processes and
systems for risk management related to the business operations as approved by the Board of
Directors.
Article 30.-Outsourced Activities
Where the AMI intends to outsource any operational functions, the AMI shall obtain prior
approval from the NBC.
7

The AMI shall remain fully liable for all its actions including any acts of the outside service
provider.
Article 31.- Conflict of Interest
The AMI shall establish policies and manage conflicts of interest to ensure all activities are
conducted with fairness, transparency, honesty and independence.
Article 32.-Whistle Blowing Procedure
The AMI shall establish Whistle Blowing Procedure, which is a procedure to manage conflict
of interest or compliance issues arising in the course of day-to-day operations by establishing
reporting procedures and set up protection mechanisms for employees whose duties are
properly fulfilled with integrity and in alignment with AMl's overall interest.
The AMI shall inform their employees promptly about the Whistle Blowing Process and
Procedure.
Chapter VIII
Sanctions and Fines
Article 33.- Disciplinary Sanctions
Any Institutions failing to comply with this Prakas shall be penalized according to Article 52 of
Law on Banking and Financial Institutions.
Article 34.- Fines
In addition to the above disciplinary sanctions, the NBC may impose fines as follows:
1. Failing to comply with the provision of Article 22 of this Prakas shall be liable to
transactional fine of KHR 1,000,000 (one million riels) per day; and
2. Failing to comply with this Prakas except item 1 of this Article shall be subject to
transactional fine of KHR 3,000,000 (three million riels) per day counting from the
deadline the NBC requires the Institution to take corrective action.
3. The AMI which does not comply with injunction and/or breach relevant regulations,
shall be fined KHR 1,000,000 (one million riels) per day starting from the effective date
determined by the NBC.
Article 35.- License Suspension or Revocation
The NBC may suspend or revoke the license, if AMI:
Does not commence its business operation within 6 (six) months after receiving the
license;
- Violates the laws or regulations;
Insolvent; or
- Voluntarily ceases its operation.
8

Chapter IX
Final Provisions
Article 36.- Implementation
The General Secretary, the General Director of Regulation and Financial Inclusion, the
General Director of Banking Supervision, the General Director of Central Banking Operation,
the General Director of Policy and International Cooperation, the General Cashier, the General
Director of Cash Management, General Inspector, Directors of all relevant Departments in the
National Bank of Cambodia, Asset Management Institution and all Banks and Financial
Institutions under the National Bank of Cambodia's supervisory authority shall strictly
implement this Prakas.
Article 37.- Effect
This Prakas shall have effect from the signing date.

The Governor
